title: Better Business Bureau warns of government shutdown scams - NewsBreak
text:
By Scott Minshall No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
BIRMINGHAM, Ala. ( WIAT ) — The Better Business Bureau is warning the public about new scams relating to the government shutdown.
Experts say scam artists are taking advantage of the federal funding freeze and could be targeting you.
“We’re seeing it here. We’re seeing across the country starting to pop up. The scammers only take a few days to figure it out,” said Carl Bates, the CEO of the Alabama Better Business Bureau.
Bates says since the shutdown began, BBB has been receiving an uptick in calls about scams.
Changes to SNAP benefits take effect in October: What to know “One example is there’s calls being made about people needing to renew their passports and we can help you go through that process since the US passport office is not handling that right now. Well, that is true. The US passport office is still renewing passports, but you don’t know that. So, you say, ‘sure, I’ll hire you for $99 or $100 to help me go through the process of renewing my passport,’ which is completely false and untrue,” said Bates.
Bates says the scammers are taking advantage of the government shutdown, but they’re not stopping with passports. He says federal employees who are furloughed have also been calling the Better Business Bureau in Alabama saying they have been the target of scams.
“They’re out of work right now,” Bates explained. “The opportunity to continue to get paid as an advance, you know, we can help you through this, through this time when you’re not going to have any money coming in by advancing your income to you. And that’s also very much probably not true. But if it is, it’s at a very high interest rate.”
Bates says if you think you could be getting targeted by a scam, you should do three things: stop, call and confirm. Stop what you’re doing, call the Better Business Bureau and confirm that it is not a scam.
